items.stem: What is the main memory advantage of a generator over returning a list?

options.text: It yields items one at a time, so the whole sequence need never be held in memory
options.rationale: Correct: a generator produces values lazily on demand, keeping memory flat regardless of length.

options.text: It sorts the items as it produces them
options.rationale: Generators do not sort; they yield in the order produced.

options.text: It runs the producing code in parallel
options.rationale: Generators are single-threaded and lazy, not parallel.

options.text: It caches every produced value for reuse
options.rationale: A plain generator does not cache; once consumed, values are gone.

items.explanation: Correct: a generator produces values lazily on demand, keeping memory flat regardless of length.

items.stem: Which are correct reasons to use functools.wraps when writing a decorator? (Select TWO)

options.text: It preserves the wrapped function's __name__ and __doc__
options.rationale: Correct: wraps copies identifying metadata to the wrapper.

options.text: It keeps introspection and debugging tools showing the original function
options.rationale: Correct: tools that read metadata then report the real function.

options.text: It makes the decorator run asynchronously
options.rationale: wraps has nothing to do with async execution.

options.text: It is required for the decorator to accept arguments
options.rationale: Parameterised decorators are a separate pattern; wraps is about metadata.

items.explanation: Correct: wraps copies identifying metadata to the wrapper.; Correct: tools that read metadata then report the real function.

items.stem: When is a metaclass the appropriate tool rather than a class decorator?

options.text: When you must customise class creation itself, such as registering or validating every subclass automatically
options.rationale: Correct: metaclasses hook into class construction, which is what per-subclass behaviour requires.

options.text: Whenever you want to add a method to a single class
options.rationale: A plain method or class decorator handles that far more simply.
Attribute speed is addressed by __slots__/descriptors, not metaclasses.
Immutability is better achieved with properties, frozen dataclasses or __slots__.

items.explanation: Correct: metaclasses hook into class construction, which is what per-subclass behaviour requires.
